title: What happens if you live in space for a year?

lines.text: If you lived in space for a whole year, what would happen to your body?
Day one, your face puffs up. Fluid floats out of your legs and into your head.
With no gravity squashing your spine, you grow. Up to three percent taller.
Then the caps on your DNA, your telomeres, get longer. Scientists expected the opposite.
Then you land. Within days, you shrink back, and most of those telomeres shorten again.
You survived. Comment what you want to know next.

experiment.note: Sample script for the fact-led format (2026-11-25). Needs a space-station set and a float pose; written for the cel prototype's vocabulary.

facts.claim: Fluid shifts headward in microgravity ('puffy face, bird legs')
Astronauts can grow up to 3% taller as spinal discs expand; Scott Kelly came back ~2 in taller and lost it within ~2 days
Kelly's telomeres lengthened in flight, then most shortened within ~48 h of landing; some ended shorter than before
